title: Ann was hours from death. Then her son used AI to save her
key_facts: Ed Patrick, an anaesthetist from Oxfordshire, was at his mother Ann's hospital bedside in Nottinghamshire in May 2026 after she began suffering serious, continuous seizures; she has Parkinson's disease and was unconscious and going into kidney failure.
Anti-seizure medicines had not worked and the hospital's registrar told him she was dying.

He used Google's Gemini AI tool to summarise recent medical journal articles and told the neurology consultant the seizures were possibly a rare effect of vitamin B6 deficiency, perhaps caused by her long-term carbidopa-levodopa treatment.

Staff gave her an intravenous vitamin B6 supplement, which appeared to stop the seizures; the consultant, Dr Bruno Gran, says activity stopped within minutes and that only 14 similar cases have ever been reported.

Doctors say clinical trials are needed and warn patients not to change their own medication without medical advice; Prof Tom Foltynie says too much B6 can also cause problems and that levels should be tested before supplements.
The US FDA earlier this year put out a memo saying certain Parkinson's drugs should carry a warning about possible links to B6 deficiency; Parkinson's UK supports more research trials.
The BBC report is listed by Google News as published on 1 Oct 2026; The Times carried its own piece on the case on 10 Oct 2026.
quote_evidence: Using AI to scour recent medical journal articles, he said he identified a vitamin deficiency linked to her Parkinson's medication as a possible cause, and staff then gave her a vitamin dose that appeared to stop the seizures.
Doctors say clinical trials are needed to understand more - and warn against patients making changes to their own medication without medical advice.
Although Parkinson's affects millions of people worldwide, only 14 similar cases have ever been reported.
why_it_matters_hint: A single case suggests checking vitamin B6 in Parkinson's patients with seizures, but doctors say trials are needed and patients should not self-medicate.
event_date: Seizures and treatment in May 2026; BBC report 1 Oct 2026 (per Google News listing); The Times piece 10 Oct 2026
